Subject: Post-call: ZenHealth security & third-party roster — next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the ZenHealth security and product leads. Below is a short recap and the asks we agreed to so we can scope the integration and prepare a mutual action plan.

Quick recap
- Integration: Redwood hosted inference (dedicated option possible) to serve protected health data for clinical decision support.
- Primary concerns you raised: SOC 2 status, HIPAA BAA, data residency, and third-party tooling that will touch PHI.

Immediate asks (action items)
1) SOC 2 status & timeline — please confirm whether you have SOC 2 Type II in place and the expected date if in progress.
2) HIPAA / BAA — confirm whether ZenHealth is a covered entity or plans to sign a BAA; if you need our BAA we can share a draft.
3) Subprocessor / third-party roster — please provide the list of cloud providers, logging/analytics vendors, CDNs, and any ML tooling vendors that will receive PHI. We attached a simple template (redwood_subprocessor_template.csv) to make this easier.
4) Data residency / retention — indicate where data will be stored (US region preferred) and retention policy for request logs and artifacts.
5) Questionnaire kick-off — we attached an initial vendor security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_initial.pdf). Please have your security lead start with sections 1–3; we’ll follow up with technical deep-dive on networking and key management.

Timing / next steps
- If you can share the roster + SOC2 timeline by EOD 3/17, we’ll scope the security review and return a checklist of any contract items (BAA, DPA, encryption confirmations) within 5 business days.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sync w/ Marissa and Priyom the week of 3/22 — suggest Tue 3/23 or Thu 3/25.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_template.csv (stub), security_questionnaire_initial.pdf (stub)

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if it speeds things up.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Neha —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers inline and a couple of attachments from our side.

- SOC 2: We are currently in the final audit stage for SOC 2 Type II; auditor expects report completion by 2027-09-15 (Q3).
- HIPAA / BAA: ZenHealth is a covered entity and we will need a signed BAA. Can Redwood provide your standard BAA?
- Subprocessors: I attached a first-pass inventory (zenhealth_acc_list.xlsx) — it includes AWS (us-east-1 primary), CloudFront, Datadog (logging), Segment, and a couple of analytics partners. We will need to clarify which of those will carry PHI.
- Data residency / retention: Primary storage in us-east-1; retention varies by data type. I’ll map specifics in the roster.

We started filling the questionnaire (a few answers are in the attached file). Two asks from our security team:
1) Does Redwood support a customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) model for dedicated deployments?
2) For hosted inference, are request logs redacted automatically for PHI fields or do we need to provide a schema for redaction?

Happy to join a follow-up next week. 3/23 looks promising for us.

—Samir

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick responses, Samir. A few clarifications from the Redwood security side and a suggested intake approach to keep this moving: 

1) BAA: We can provide a standard BAA and have our legal team start a draft once you confirm the required signatories. Priyom, I’ll loop you to help expedite.
2) Customer-managed KMS: For Redwood Dedicated we support BYOK (AWS KMS integration); for hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can discuss a VPC-private plan for key material for sensitive workloads.
3) Log redaction: Our hosted product can do schema-driven redaction; we’ll need an example request payload or a list of fields to redact. For Dedicated we can also restrict logging to non-PHI by configuration.
4) Subprocessor template: Please use the attached redwood_subprocessor_template.csv — provide provider name, role (storage/logging/analytics), whether it will process PHI, region, and contact. This lets us triage high-risk vendors first.

Suggested intake workflow (to minimize back-and-forth)
- You (ZenHealth) complete the CSV with vendor roles + mark PHI processing flags.
- We (Redwood Security) review and send a short red-flag list (3–4 items max) within 3 business days.
- Contract items (BAA/DPA) to be handled by legal in parallel once red flags are known.

I’ll own the technical deep-dive. For the 30-min sync please include someone who can share a network diagram and the KMS approach. Proposed slots: Tue 3/23 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 3/25 11:00–11:30 PT.

Thanks — I’ve attached the redwood_subprocessor_template.csv to make it easier for you to respond.

Marissa Cole
